headline: New income tax structure doubles burden on middle-class, rich get relief
summary: The new income tax framework raises the tax-free income limit to BDT 4 lakh but doubles the tax rate for the subsequent income slab, significantly impacting the lower-middle and middle-class. Simultaneously, the highest income bracket sees tax benefits, shifti
details: Bangladesh's new income tax structure is set to increase the burden on lower-middle and middle-class individuals, while the wealthy are receiving tax benefits. For the current fiscal year, the tax-free income limit has been raised to BDT 4 lakh, up from BDT 3.5 lakh previously.

However, the tax rate for the income slab immediately following the tax-free limit has been doubled, despite the increase in the exemption threshold. In the recently concluded fiscal year, income up to BDT 1 lakh above the BDT 3.5 lakh tax-free limit was taxed at 5%.

Under the new framework, income between BDT 4 lakh and BDT 7 lakh (the next BDT 3 lakh) will now be taxed at 10%, a substantial increase. This change is expected to bring a significant number of lower-middle-class individuals into a higher tax bracket, increasing their overall tax liability.

Dr. Khondaker Golam Moazzem, Research Director at the Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD), noted that while the highest income slab's tax rate remains 30% for the current year, it is slated to increase to 35% from the next fiscal year. He highlighted that the government has provided tax relief to the wealthy in this year's budget.

Moazzem emphasized that the primary objective of increasing the minimum tax exemption is to protect citizens from the effects of inflation. However, he warned that the new income tax system is likely to put considerable financial pressure on a large segment of the country's population.

The new budget introduces various tax exemptions in certain sectors while simultaneously expanding the tax net in other areas. The National Board of Revenue (NBR) faces the challenge of achieving a substantial revenue target under these revised policies.

headline: Israel announces new illegal settlements in West Bank & Gaza, allocates $400M+ ahead of election
summary: The plan includes three new settlements in Gaza and expansion in the West Bank, drawing criticism from Israeli elites and the UN, who deem settler violence as state violence.
details: Israeli Defence and Finance Ministers have announced plans for new illegal settlements in Gaza and expanded construction in the West Bank, allocating over $400 million. This comes ahead of Israel's national election on October 27, as Netanyahu's right-wing coalition seeks to increase control over occupied Palestinian territories.

Defence Minister Israel Katz detailed plans for three new "military settlements" in northern Gaza, a method used for decades to pave the way for civilian settlements. Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich announced 1.3 billion shekels (approximately $350 million) for over 12 new Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.

The funding for West Bank settlements was reportedly approved last month but kept secret due to potential US opposition. Israeli military commander Major General Avi Bluth praised illegal settlers as "security partners," speaking at a meeting for the "Farms Association," which represents settlements illegal even under Israeli law.

These settlements are instrumental in displacing Palestinians from their homes and land across the occupied West Bank. Former prime ministers and heads of security agencies have threatened legal action against government support for settler violence.

The UN Human Rights Office recently reported that settler violence is effectively "state violence," detailing how Israel uses settlers to annex Palestinian territory. The report notes that the lack of prosecution for perpetrators fuels unchecked violence.

Dror Etkes, founder of Kerem Navot, an organization monitoring Israeli land seizure, stated that illegal settlements are not built for long-term military use. He explained that the military phase is merely the first step to facilitate future civilian settlements, a pattern seen in dozens of West Bank settlements since 1967.

Deputy Chief of Staff Major General Tamir Yadai informed Defence Minister Katz that Israel now controls 65% of Gaza. He stated that over 70,000 Gazans, including 21,000 children, have been killed. This leaves nearly 2 million Palestinians crowded into the remaining one-third of Gaza, following a destructive war mediated by former US President Donald Trump last year.
